subject: Post-call recap: model matching framework & next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Roberts <elaine@finlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: model matching framework & next steps

Hi Elaine — thanks again for your time today. Short recap and a proposed path forward from our side.

TL;DR
- Goal: Get a deterministic evaluation for "parity" vs your incumbent baseline (FinBase v3) and decide a go/no-go for a limited production pilot.
- Acceptance target we discussed: >=95% relative on task accuracy + <=5% delta in hallucination incidents on our labelled eval set (see attached CSV).
- Proposed pilots: two open-model candidates + Redwood baseline variant delivered by our runtime.

What we heard you say
- Primary KPIs: factual accuracy on financial Q&A, hallucination rate, and response latency p95 under your 200 qps simulated load.
- Constraints: no external retention of PII for trial, SSO access for 3 reviewers, procurement window ~4–6 weeks.

Redwood recommended trial plan (week 0–4)
1) Benchmarks & prompt set (attached): run the attached prompt_set_v1.json against the baseline and the open models. We provided finlytics_benchmark_summary.csv as a sample of metrics we can compute.
2) Models to trial (shortlist):
   - Mistral-40B (8-bit) — strong instruction-following baseline, good throughput/latency tradeoff.
   - Llama-3-70B (4-bit quantized) — higher capacity option; may improve factual recall on long-context Q&A.
   - Redwood-verified baseline (medium-sized optimized variant) — to assess parity vs your current commercial baseline.
3) Metrics we will compute: exact-match / F1 for structured Q&A, hallucination incidence (annotated), latency p50/p95/p99, and token-cost per response.
4) Regression guardrails: we will run a small human annotation sweep (50–100 samples) for each candidate to detect quality regressions early.

Operational notes & asks for you
- Please confirm the four reviewers who need sandbox access and whether SSO (SAML) is mandatory for them.
- Confirm the dataset slices you most care about (e.g., earnings calls, SEC filings, customer invoices).
- Preferable timeline: start the sandbox run Mon 10/26; deliver initial metrics by Fri 11/6.

Attachments included: finlytics_benchmark_summary.csv, prompt_set_v1.json. I also attached a brief SSO scoping doc for your infra team.

Next steps I propose
- You confirm reviewers + SSO requirement (reply all).
- We provision a sandbox instance and drop the prompt set & runner (internal step).
- Follow-up sync: 30 min evaluation check-in the week of 11/2 — Monica will propose times.

Thanks — happy to adjust if you want a different model shortlist or acceptance thresholds.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Rachel.kim@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

--

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Cc: Elaine Roberts <elaine@finlytics.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 18:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model matching framework & next steps

Rachel — solid recap. A few technical clarifications and operational notes from infra/serving: 

1) Model configs to try (runtime notes)
   - Mistral-40B: start with bf16/8-bit quant (weight-only) on a 2-GPU pool; batch target 24–32 for latency control. Expected p95 ~350–550ms depending on prompt length.
   - Llama-3-70B (4-bit): prefer quant aware runtime; enable KV-cache reuse for multi-turn Q&A to reduce token cost. Expect higher p95 but better factuality on long contexts.
   - Redwood baseline: our medium-optimized variant (int8, kernel fusion) — useful to sanity-check cost vs quality.

2) Evaluation harness
   - We'll run the prompt_set_v1.json inside our internal runner and compute the metrics you outlined. I recommend adding a small adversarial subset (10–20 prompts designed to surface hallucinations).

3) Data controls
   - For sandbox: we will disable retention (14-day auto-delete) and exclude logs from the hosted metrics dump if FinLytics requires that. SSO scoping doc outlines the options.

4) Procurement & Dedicated ask
   - If they express interest in Dedicated, we should capture expected 95th% qps and SLA needs now — will affect cost estimates.

I will prepare the runner config and a short README for the reviewers to run the jobs. Monica — can you own scheduling the eval sync?

- Dylan
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model matching framework & next steps

Hi Rachel / team — thanks for the clear plan. A few items from our side: 

1) Reviewers & access
   - Confirmed reviewers: Elaine Roberts (product), Marcus Liu (data science), and Tara Shah (infra). SSO is required (SAML) — our infra team will send metadata after we sign MNDA.

2) Acceptance thresholds
   - The 95% relative accuracy target sounds reasonable as a starting point, but we need more clarity on how hallucination rate is measured. Can you confirm the definition and the annotation instructions you plan to use? We cannot accept models that increase hallucination incidents for regulatory Q&A above our baseline.

3) Timeline
   - The proposed sandbox start (10/26) works. We need initial metrics and an annotated sample by 11/6. If the open models approach parity, we will open a procurement conversation for Dedicated capacity (expecting to roughly match our current committed spend).

4) Security/compliance
   - Legal will need the SOC 2 evidence and data flow diagram. Please route those to legal@finlytics.com.

5) Pricing question
   - Can you provide a ballpark price range for a 3-month Dedicated pilot (monthly commit) vs hosted consumption for the same expected qps? A rough estimate is fine for now.

Thanks — look forward to the sandbox.
